finding.headline: The public pieces for crash-safe outer evaluation are now individually source-bound, but no audited system in this run composes all of them. cap-evolve has post-score consumption detection, Koboi has a durable pre-call running marker, Swiss-AI has missing-cell resume, while Auto-Research exposes a concrete certify-order counterexample that re-queries holdout before checking the prior certificate.

cap_evolve.explicit_second_look_incident: Current RunDir.begin_test_attempt documents a real run where finalize was killed by a foreground timeout after test had already been scored; retry scored test again and the reported number became the second look. PR #366 records the same incident as the motivation for the guard.
cap_evolve.current_guard: Before a finalize attempt, begin_test_attempt checks the unused seal and scans rollouts/test/*.json. If any test rollout exists while the seal is uncommitted, retry is refused unless CAPEVOLVE_ALLOW_TEST_RESCORE is explicitly set.
cap_evolve.remaining_pre_first_outcome_gap: evaluate_candidate reserves the test seal before evaluation but creates no content-bound durable logical evaluation intent. run_target/run_batch/run_trials can therefore dispatch/complete remotely before _persist_trial writes the first local rollout. A hard kill in that interval leaves no test rollout, so retry is allowed and can repeat the same held-out evaluation.
cap_evolve.batch_amplification: For run_batch/run_trials the uncertain interval can include an entire returned batch because per-cell scoring/persistence happens only after the batch call returns.
cap_evolve.partial_resume_gap: Once any local test rollout exists, begin_test_attempt fail-closes the whole subsequent finalize. This prevents a second look but does not resume only missing test cells.
structural_outer_gaps: Open issue #361 documents that direct harness.evaluate_candidate(split='test') can score test outside finalize and leave the seal unburned, bricking the later legitimate finalize.

Open issue #341 documents that CAPEVOLVE_ALLOW_TEST_RESCORE claims its use is recorded in the run, but the current code does not persist/event/report the override, so a deliberate second look can be undisclosed.

koboi_bridge.useful_mechanism: StepJournal.record_step eagerly commits a 'running' row before each LLM call, so a crash leaves a durable pre-call marker; resume marks such rows interrupted. Its crash benchmark resumes a fresh agent and re-executes only missing tool calls after an in-process mid-turn interruption.
koboi_bridge.scope_limit: The benchmark uses idempotent tracking tools and explicitly says a literal cross-process SIGKILL harness is future work. The step identity shown is session/turn/step, not a semantic request digest bound to a provider idempotency token. The HTTP IdempotencyRegistry is in-memory TTL only, so this is not provider-exactly-once evaluation authority by itself.

autoresearch_counterexample.strength: The project separates inner-CV search from an explicit outer holdout certification command, freezes the selected source hash, runs evaluators in fresh subprocesses, and writes a holdout_certification.json artifact.
autoresearch_counterexample.second_query_bug: CampaignRunner.certify() calls evaluator.holdout(workspace) before it checks whether holdout_certification.json already exists. If the file exists, it compares the newly computed payload to the old one only after the second holdout evaluation has already occurred.
autoresearch_counterexample.test_confirms_repeat: tests/test_runner.py calls CampaignRunner(config).certify() twice and only asserts matching source hashes, so the current regression test explicitly permits repeated holdout execution rather than proving cache-only second access.
autoresearch_counterexample.trial_resume_limit: RUNBOOK says an interrupted trial directory remains for audit and next launch chooses a new trial ID. run_one appends TrialRecord only after agent execution/evaluation, so there is no durable logical trial/evaluation outcome record before the external command.

swiss_ai_cell_resume_component.mechanism: launch_evaluations_gracefuly.sh reconstructs a COMPLETED_MAP from per-task result directories/requested_tasks manifests, computes MISSING_TASKS, and launches only missing groups; --force_tasks deliberately removes matches from COMPLETED_MAP to re-evaluate them.
swiss_ai_cell_resume_component.scope_limit: This is a useful missing-cell resume pattern, not a one-shot terminal outer-evaluation authority and not a pre-dispatch content-bound WAL.

minimal_composed_protocol: Freeze candidate source hash, evaluator/config digest, dataset/split digest, ordered test cell manifest, and an attempt_id before OUTER access.
Atomically persist OuterEvaluationIntent(attempt_id, semantic_request_digest, cell_manifest, status=PLANNED) before any evaluator/provider call.

For each cell, derive stable cell_id from attempt_id plus task/trial identity; bind dispatch to a deterministic provider token when supported, otherwise persist DISPATCHING/UNKNOWN and require reconciliation rather than blind retry.
Persist each cell outcome immutably and conflict-check same cell_id against the semantic digest; restart derives completed/missing cells from the log and dispatches only provably missing cells.
Derive aggregate and certificate entirely from the immutable cell log; write certificate before terminal seal transition or complete both through a recoverable state machine.
On later certify/read calls, check terminal certificate/attempt state before any evaluator access and return the cached certificate only. Never call holdout and then compare with cache.
Make OUTER evaluator/data access capability-gated below all generic evaluation APIs, so alternate callers cannot bypass finalize/certify.
If exceptional second-look override exists, persist a non-erasable disclosure event before dispatch, bind it into report metadata, and never present its score as an independent holdout.
falsification_tests: SIGKILL immediately before provider dispatch: retry performs exactly one logical outer evaluation.
SIGKILL after provider accepts but before local response: retry uses same provider token or enters UNKNOWN/reconcile; no blind second dispatch.
SIGKILL after first local cell: restart completes only missing cells and never reruns persisted cells.
SIGKILL after an arbitrary subset of batch cells: restart's completed/missing partition is deterministic from the immutable log.
SIGKILL after aggregate/certificate write but before terminal seal: restart commits/reconciles from cached evidence without evaluator access.
Call certify twice: instrumented holdout evaluator invocation count remains exactly one.
Call generic evaluate(test) outside finalize/certify: core rejects before touching evaluator/data.
Change candidate/evaluator/dataset/split under same attempt_id: fail closed as semantic-id conflict.
Use second-look override: disclosure is durable before dispatch and appears in machine-readable and human report outputs.
search_result_scope: Targeted public source/issue search in this invocation did not find a single audited self-improver that simultaneously implements pre-dispatch content-bound evaluation WAL, provider reconciliation, cell-level partial resume, and mechanically cache-only/non-queryable OUTER. This is a scoped negative result, not a repository-universe impossibility claim.
exact_next_action: On the next fresh-control invocation, first test whether Auto-Research-AI-Scientist has a newer branch/PR fixing certify-before-cache ordering or adding a durable certification attempt state. Then search evaluation services/workflow engines for a content-bound pre-dispatch evaluation/cell WAL with missing-cell resume. Prioritize an implementation where a second certify call is demonstrably cache-only (evaluator invocation count stays one), and where generic evaluation APIs cannot query OUTER outside the terminal authority. If none exists, build a minimal executable reference state machine from the six kill boundaries in this contract and test it with real cross-process SIGKILL.
